newsitem.title: USA: Pryor McClendon says reorganizing operations.
newsitem.headline: Pryor McClendon says reorganizing operations.

text.p: Philadelphia-based Pryor McClendon Counts & Co said Thursday it is reorganizing operations in a move that includes some layoffs and salary reductions in the municipal area.
"The market is not what it was in '93. Everybody is looking at cost structure," Allen Counts, the brokerage and trading firm's president, said in an interview.
But Counts stressed that Pryor has no intention of exiting the municipal bond business. "We have bright hopes for the municipal side, so we'll be around," Counts said.
The company's president said there had been "a couple of layoffs" that were felt "across the board" in the firm's Philadelphia, New York and Atlanta offices.
Non-municipal operations were affected as well, he said.
"We grew so fast during the boom years," Counts said. "We're making people more accountable about their existence."
